nodes.label: Alexander Cunningham
nodes.subject: history
nodes.detail: First Director-General of the Archaeological Survey of India (ASI), often called the father of Indian archaeology. Noted brick-robbing at Harappa in 1875. Focused on the Early Historic period (6th c. BCE onwards) and missed the true antiquity of Harappan artefacts initially.

nodes.label: John Marshall
nodes.subject: history
nodes.detail: Director-General of ASI who announced the discovery of the Indus Valley Civilisation to the world in 1924. First professional archaeologist to work in India. Credited with making India "three thousand years older" by establishing Harappan antiquity. However, his horizontal excavation method ignored stratigraphy, losing chronological detail.

nodes.label: R.E.M. Wheeler
nodes.subject: history
nodes.detail: Director-General of ASI from 1944. Introduced stratigraphic excavation methods to Indian archaeology, rectifying Marshall's approach. Excavated at Harappa in 1946. Initially proposed the (now-discredited) Aryan invasion theory for Harappan decline based on skeletal evidence.
